introduction:
In Karnataka, property registration (Sale Deed Registration) is a mandatory legal process governed by the Registration Act, 1908. It establishes legal ownership, secures title rights, and protects against future land disputes.

The process is managed online through the Kaveri Online Services (Kaveri 2.0) portal and finalized with a mandatory in-person visit to the local Sub-Registrar Office (SRO) for biometric verification and final deed execution.
quickFacts:
Important to Know
  • Service: Sale Deed Registration for properties in Bangalore, Karnataka.
  • Portal: Kaveri Online Services (Kaveri 2.0).
  • Timeframe: Online application SRO validation takes about 24 hours. The physical registration at the SRO takes approximately 20-30 minutes.
  • Mandatory Physical Visit: The buyer, seller, and two witnesses must physically visit the designated SRO on the booked slot to complete the registration. Walk-ins without pre-booked slots are not allowed.
documentsRequired:
Documents Required for Property Registration

Note: Keep the original documents and two sets of self-attested photocopies ready for SRO verification.
Deed & Agreements
  • Executed Sale Deed: The original foundational legal document signed by the seller, buyer, and two witnesses.
  • Previous Title Deeds: Copy of the seller's previously registered deed.
  • Sale Agreement: Original Sale Agreement (if applicable).
Property & ID Details
  • Property Details: E-Khata and latest Property Tax Receipt.
  • ID Proofs: Aadhaar Card, PAN Card, or Passport for the buyer, seller, and all witnesses.
Special Case Approvals
  • Power of Attorney (POA): Required if the buyer or seller is being represented by an agent (e.g., NRI sellers).
  • TDS Payment Proof: Required if the property consideration amount exceeds ₹50 Lakhs or if the seller is an NRI.
Witnesses
  • Two independent witnesses.
  • Original ID proofs (Aadhaar/Voter ID) and passport-size photos.
onlineApplication:
Phase 1: Online Pre-Registration (Kaveri 2.0)

Pre-registration and fee payment must be processed online through the Kaveri 2.0 portal before visiting the SRO.

Step-by-Step Process:
  1. Registration & Login: Visit the Kaveri Online Services Portal, create an account, and log in.
  2. Initiate Application: Click on Start a New Application and select Document Registration.
  3. Document Details: Choose the Nature of Document as Sale, Article as Conveyance, and select the appropriate Sub-article (e.g., Sale/Conveyance of Immovable Property Converted Land/Site/Building/Apartment).
  4. Property Search: Select the property type (e.g., Non-Agricultural). Choose the jurisdiction (like E-Aasthi for BBMP limits). Enter your 10-digit E-Aasthi PID, ward number, and village to auto-fetch the property details. Save and continue.
  5. Property Schedule: Verify the auto-populated property dimensions, boundaries, and description.
  6. Party Details:
    - Executant (Seller): Enter the seller's details, verify their Aadhaar, and input contact info. Add multiple executants if there are joint sellers. If a POA is involved, input the POA holder's details and upload the POA document.
    - Presenter (Buyer): Enter the buyer's details, verify their Aadhaar, and assign them as the "Presenter".
    - Identifiers (Witnesses): Enter the details of two witnesses along with their Aadhaar verification. Link each witness to the respective buyer or seller they are identifying.
  7. Market Valuation: Input property specifics (flat number, floor, amenities, parking, etc.) to calculate the government guidance value and market valuation.
  8. Fee Calculation: Enter the actual consideration (sale) amount. If you already paid stamp duty during the Sale Agreement phase via an e-Stamp, enter the e-Stamp number to offset that amount. The system will auto-calculate the final Stamp Duty, Registration Fee, Scanning Fee, etc.
  9. Submit for Approval: Review the complete application summary and submit it. The status will update to Pending at SRO.
  10. Make Payment & Book Slot: Once the Sub-Registrar validates the application (usually within 24 hours), the status will change to Pending for Payment. Pay the fees online (Netbanking/UPI). After successful payment, click Book Slot to choose a convenient date and time for your physical appointment.
offlineApplication:
Phase 2: The Physical SRO Execution

In Karnataka, the Kaveri 2.0 portal is strictly mandatory for the initial stages of property registration. You cannot submit a completely offline, paper-based application. However, the final execution is an offline process.

Step-by-Step Process:
  1. Physical Visit: On the scheduled date, the buyer, seller, and both witnesses must visit the selected Sub-Registrar Office.
  2. Carry Documents: Bring all original documents, ID proofs, the printed Kaveri application summary, and payment receipts.
  3. Verification & Biometrics: SRO officers will verify the physical files. Digital biometrics (fingerprints) and photographs will be captured to conclude the registration.
  4. Deed Execution: All parties sign the physical registry to finalize the transfer of the property title.
afterApplying:
Post-Registration — EC Verification

After the physical registration is complete, you should download the Encumbrance Certificate (EC) to verify that the transaction has been recorded in the government books.

How to Download the EC:
  1. Go to the Kaveri portal home page and click Start a New Application > Encumbrance Certificate (Online EC).
  2. Search for your property using the 10-digit E-Aasthi PID.
  3. Select the period of search (from the date of the previous seller's deed to the current date).
  4. Locate your recent sale transaction in the search results and copy the Registration Number.
  5. Proceed to apply for a signed EC, paste your Registration Number, pay the nominal fee (approx. ₹150), and download the digitally signed Encumbrance Certificate in PDF format.
